entries.title: Ripley Scroll (Wellcome b18597762) — Section 1 — Opening Section
entries.creator: English alchemical tradition (Ripley circle)
entries.medium: manuscript on vellum, pen and watercolor
entries.summary:
A second Wellcome Ripley Scroll witness (Wellcome Library b18597762), photographed in 14 IIIF sections via the Wellcome Collection. This parchment roll preserves the Ripley Scroll iconographic tradition — the canonical English alchemical scroll attributed to George Ripley (c.1415–1490) and his circle — in a distinct manuscript copy with variant compositional choices compared to the WT303 copy.

## Iconography

Like all Ripley Scrolls, this manuscript narrates the alchemical Great Work through a sequence of emblematic paintings on parchment: the philosopher-alchemist bearing the scroll of the Work; corrosion scenes (green lion, toad/eagle); the philosophical conjunction of Sol and Luna; the pelican of multiplication; and the progressive stages of the Work through nigredo (black), albedo (white), citrinitas (yellow), and rubedo (red) to the final triumphant Red King. Sections 1–7 (heavier file weights at 145–157KB) preserve the illustrated panels; sections 8–14 are predominantly verse text.

## Significance

This second Wellcome witness allows comparative study with the WT303 copy, illuminating how different scribes and artists adapted the standard Ripley Scroll program for different patrons. Jennifer Rampling (*The Experimental Fire*) has systematically analyzed the corpus of surviving Ripley Scrolls, demonstrating how the tradition transmitted and transformed Ripley's alchemical poetics across a century and a half of English alchemy.

## For artists & game designers

The slightly different proportions (several canvases are notably wider than WT303) suggest variant panel sizing — offering alternative aspect ratios for game card design. The first seven illustrated sections provide a directly usable sequence of emblematic images for character art, level-select screens, or tarot-style card decks.
